label: Compliant plan (should pass every check)

a.text: A revolving four-year plan (1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029) covering two initiatives: Initiative 1, local drilling-fluid additive substitution (2026 to 2028), and Initiative 2, a follow-on field pilot (2028 to 2029). The plan is reviewed and rolled forward at each six-monthly update.

b.text: Purpose: reduce dependence on imported drilling-fluid additives and build Nigerian technical capacity in drilling-fluid formulation. Expected outcome: Qualify at least three locally sourced additive blends that meet API Spec 13A performance limits at no more than 70% of the imported-additive cost, and replace at least 30% of imported additive volume in the Company's onshore wells by 31 December 2028.

c.text: Initiative 1 characterises, treats and blends Nigerian barite and bentonite and tests the blends in the laboratory and in two field trials. Initiative 2 (outline only) extends field use to six further wells. Objectives: (1) characterise six local deposits; (2) formulate and qualify blends; (3) validate them in the field; (4) train Nigerian personnel.

d.text: Research scope: advanced (applied). Laboratory formulation and field validation, building on published characterisation work.

e.text: Planned expenditure over the plan period is ₦64.0 million, shown by year in the table below.

f.text: Standard laboratory fluid testing to API Spec 13A and API RP 13B-1 procedures (density, rheology, fluid loss), in the research centre's accredited laboratory. Equipment: rotational viscometer, HPHT filter press, mud balance. The procedures align with internationally accepted API standards.

g.text: Material sampling at named deposits in Bayelsa and Rivers States; laboratory work at the research centre, Port Harcourt; field trials at two Company onshore wells (Sample Field-1 and Sample Field-2, Rivers State).

h.text: Initiative 1: 36 months (1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028). Initiative 2: 24 months (1 January 2028 to 31 December 2029).

i.text: Sponsoring institution: Niger Delta Institute of Applied Petroleum Research, Port Harcourt (fictional). Director: Prof. Chidi Eze-Sample. Officer in charge of the research: Dr. Ada Okeke-Sample.

j.text: Laboratory waste is handled under the institute's waste protocol and field trials follow the Company's approved mud-management plan. Each blend is tested for toxicity and biodegradability. Local sourcing is expected to cut the transport emissions of imported additives. Findings go to the steering team.

k.text: The Company proposes that the Board nominate a representative to the steering team, receive quarterly progress reports, and attend each field trial and the final review.

l.text: The Company will issue a public call for field-pilot partners for Initiative 2, open to Nigerian universities and research centres, in the first quarter of 2028.

m.text: The Head of Technical Services (Dr. Bola Adeyemi-Sample) leads delivery. Key officers: the Drilling Fluids Engineer and the Local Content Officer. The research centre carries out the laboratory work under the Principal Investigator.

n.text: Methodology and requirements: material sampling and characterisation, blend formulation, laboratory qualification, field validation and cost comparison. Requirements are access to the accredited laboratory, two trial wells and a dedicated data analyst.

o.text: Eight Company engineers and six research-centre technicians trained in fluid formulation and testing; two MSc students attached to the project; one three-month industrial attachment each year.

p.text: Phase 1 (2026): material characterisation and formulation. Phase 2 (2027): laboratory qualification. Phase 3 (2028): field trials and cost review. Phase 4 (2028 to 2029): Initiative 2 pilot. Milestones and indicators are in Annex 1, sections 5 and 6.

expected_outcome_text: Qualify at least three locally sourced additive blends that meet API Spec 13A performance limits at no more than 70% of the imported-additive cost, and replace at least 30% of imported additive volume in the Company's onshore wells by 31 December 2028.

project.title: Substitution of Imported Drilling-Fluid Additives with Locally Sourced Barite and Bentonite Blends for Niger Delta Wells
project.goals_and_objectives: Characterise six Nigerian barite and bentonite deposits; formulate and qualify at least three blends against API Spec 13A; validate the best blends in two onshore wells; compare cost against imported additives; train Nigerian engineers and technicians. The project addresses the cost and supply risk of imported additives and builds local formulation capacity.

kpis.indicator: At least three blends meet API Spec 13A limits by 30 June 2027
Two trials completed by 30 June 2028; fluid-loss and rheology within limits
Cost at or below 70% of imported additives; 14 personnel trained by 31 December 2028
